| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Change where All_Changes.action=created All_Changes.object_category=pod All_Changes.user="*enterprise-gateway*" by All_Changes.object, All_Changes.user, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | join type=inner object [ search index=k8s_audit sourcetype="kube:apiserver:audit" verb=created objectRef.resource=pods "user.username"="*enterprise-gateway*" "requestObject.spec.volumes{}.hostPath.path"=* | rename objectRef.name as object | eval host_paths=mvjoin('requestObject.spec.volumes{}.hostPath.path', ",") | table object, host_paths, sourceIPs{} ] | sort - _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Change where All_Changes.action=created All_Changes.object_category=pod All_Changes.user="*enterprise-gateway*" by All_Changes.object, All_Changes.user, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | join type=inner object [ search index=k8s_audit sourcetype="kube:apiserver:audit" verb=created objectRef.resource=pods "user.username"="*enterprise-gateway*" "requestObject.spec.volumes{}.hostPath.path"=* | rename objectRef.name as object | eval host_paths=mvjoin('requestObject.spec.volumes{}.hostPath.path', ",") | table object, host_paths, sourceIPs{} ] | sort - _time
Cron/persistence file written on Kubernetes worker node from container runtime context AIInstallation Medium
Detects creation or modification of /etc/cron* or /var/spool/cron/* files on Kubernetes worker nodes — the article's explicit post-escape persistence vector after the CVE-2026-44180 UID bypass + hostPath mount. Kernel pods exist to run user code, not to schedule host-level cron jobs; any cron-file write on a worker node is investigation-worthy. Rationale: Article PoC explicitly recommends 'creating a crontab entry in the mounted host file system' as the worker-node escape outcome. Filters specifically on container-runtime-spawned writes (runc / containerd-shim) because legitimate cron edits on a K8s worker should come from configuration-management agents (cloud-init, Ansible, Puppet) or package installs — not from runc. Cross-checked the article's mount-namespace escape pattern against MITRE T1611 / T1053.003. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-chq7-94j8-cj28 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1053.003 T1611
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cloud-init or kubeadm node bootstrap writing /etc/cron.d/kubeadm at first boot
  • Ansible/Puppet/Salt configuration-management agents updating cron jobs on worker nodes during routine rollout
  • Package manager (apt/yum/dnf) post-install scripts dropping logrotate or sysstat cron entries
  • Operator manually editing crontab over SSH for break-glass diagnostics
  • Container image build caches on the node side-effecting /var/lib/containerd writes that get mis-attributed
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in ("cloud-init","ansible","puppet","salt","chef-client")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "apt-get" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "dpkg" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "yum" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "dnf"
Response runbook
Triage: dump the cron file contents (`cat /etc/cron.d/*`, `crontab -l` for each user) on the affected worker node and identify the new entry; pull the parent process tree to confirm the writer chained back to a containerd-shim → kernel-* container. Contain: cordon and drain the worker node, remove the malicious cron entry, kill the offending kernel pod, and rotate the kubelet credentials on that node (treat the node as compromised). Hunt: across all worker nodes, search for cron entries created in the same window with similar command lines (curl|sh, reverse-shell one-liners, base64 payloads), enumerate any new SSH keys under /root/.ssh and /home/*/.ssh, check /etc/passwd for new users, and pivot to UC2/UC3 to find the originating kernel pod.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron."
     or FolderPath == "/var/spool/cron"
     or FolderPath startswith "/var/spool/cron/"
     or (FolderPath == "/etc" and FileName in ("crontab","anacrontab"))
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSPlatform, MachineGroup, AdditionalFields) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| where OSPlatform in ("Linux","Ubuntu","RedHat","CentOS","Debian","SUSE")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/run/containerd","/var/lib/docker","/var/lib/containerd","/usr/bin/runc","/usr/sbin/runc")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("runc","containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2","crun","kata-runtime")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("runc","containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2","crun")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.daily/","/etc/cron.hourly/","/etc/cron.weekly/","/etc/cron.monthly/","/var/spool/cron/")
     or TargetFilePath in ("/etc/crontab","/etc/anacrontab")
| extend ParentIsRuntime = ActingProcessName has_any ("runc","containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2","crun","kata-runtime")
| where ParentIsRuntime or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/run/containerd","/var/lib/containerd","/var/lib/docker")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cron Persistence Written from Container Runtime Context on K8s Worker
id: 8c2f1a47-d931-4e58-92a6-1f7b3c4d2e95
description: Detects writes to host cron paths on Kubernetes worker nodes whose initiating process is the container runtime (runc / containerd-shim) — a post-escape persistence step described in CVE-2026-44180 (Jupyter Enterprise Gateway hostPath + root-UID bypass).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-chq7-94j8-cj28
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1053.003
  - attack.t1611
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - '/etc/cron.d/'
      - '/etc/cron.daily/'
      - '/etc/cron.hourly/'
      - '/etc/cron.weekly/'
      - '/etc/cron.monthly/'
      - '/var/spool/cron/'
  selection_file:
    TargetFilename:
      - '/etc/crontab'
      - '/etc/anacrontab'
  selection_runtime:
    Image|contains:
      - 'runc'
      - 'containerd-shim'
      - 'crun'
      - 'kata-runtime'
  condition: (selection_path or selection_file) and selection_runtime
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(PATH OR SYSCALL) (@file.path:/etc/cron.d/* OR @file.path:/etc/cron.daily/* OR @file.path:/etc/cron.hourly/* OR @file.path:/etc/cron.weekly/* OR @file.path:/etc/cron.monthly/* OR @file.path:/var/spool/cron/* OR @file.path:/etc/crontab OR @file.path:/etc/anacrontab) (@process.executable.path:*runc* OR @process.executable.path:*containerd-shim* OR @process.executable.path:*crun* OR @process.command_line:*\/run\/containerd*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/^\/(etc\/(cron(tab|\.(d|daily|hourly|weekly|monthly))|anacrontab)|var\/spool\/cron)/i
| ContextImageFileName=/(runc|containerd-shim|crun|kata-runtime)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
| count > 0
CLOUD

| tstats summariesonly=t count, values(Filesystem.process_name) as procs, values(Filesystem.user) as users from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("/etc/crontab","/etc/anacrontab") OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.d/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.daily/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.hourly/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.weekly/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.monthly/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/var/spool/cron/*") Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","written") by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.file_path, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search dest IN ("*worker*","*node*","*k8s*","*kube*") OR procs IN ("runc","containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2") | sort - _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Filesystem.process_name) as procs, values(Filesystem.user) as users from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("/etc/crontab","/etc/anacrontab") OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.d/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.daily/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.hourly/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.weekly/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/cron.monthly/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/var/spool/cron/*") Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","written") by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.file_path, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search dest IN ("*worker*","*node*","*k8s*","*kube*") OR procs IN ("runc","containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2") | sort - _time
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High

Argamal COM Hijack of Windows Color System Calibration Loader CLSID AIInstallation High
Detects HKCU CLSID hijack of the Windows Color System Calibration Loader {B210D694-C8DF-490D-9576-9E20CDBC20BD} or the Stage1 staging CLSID {722D0F89-B69C-4700-AE8C-4A44350E4876} where InprocServer32 / ShellFolder points to a DLL in AppData\Local. This is Argamal's login-trigger persistence anchor. Rationale: Anchored on the two exact CLSIDs from the article ({B210D694-...} Calibration Loader and {722D0F89-...} Stage1 staging) plus the HKCU AppData\Local InprocServer32 payload location — the combination is article-specific and not produced by any legitimate Color System software (which writes HKLM).
ATT&CKT1546.015 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Color-calibration software (DisplayCAL, X-Rite i1Profiler) registering color-management COM objects — but these write HKLM, not HKCU AppData\Local
  • Per-user installers from non-vetted vendors creating CLSID overrides under HKCU
  • Developer machines registering test COM objects in user profile during build/debug
  • DRM or anti-cheat agents that legitimately COM-hijack (rare; investigate parent process)
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("displaycalGUI.exe","i1ProfilerTray.exe","basICColor.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "Program Files")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the writing process (InitiatingProcessFileName/CommandLine), confirm it is NOT a known color-calibration vendor and that RegistryValueData resolves to a random-named DLL inside AppData\Local. Hash the target DLL and check VT / EDR verdict. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host, kill any taskhostw.exe/explorer.exe instance currently loading the rogue DLL, delete the HKCU CLSID override, and delete the staged DLL. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the host for the natives2_blob.bin loader, MI_V/MI_V2 env vars, bitsadmin transfers of zaesdl.dat, and UDP/57441 or TCP/3747 to 186.158.223.35. Pull the originating game executable and its modified ffmpeg.dll (SHA1 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) for IR.
DeviceRegistryEvents

Argamal MI_V / MI_V2 Environment Variable Stage Handoff AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the HKCU\Environment\MI_V or MI_V2 value used by Argamal Stage1 PowerShell to hand off the Base64-encoded Stage2 payload to a delayed scheduled task. The variable name is unique to this family. Rationale: MI_V / MI_V2 is a unique-to-Argamal env-var name documented in the Securelist write-up as the Stage1→Stage2 handoff. Anchored on the exact HKCU\Environment subkey + literal value names — no legitimate software writes these names.
ATT&CKT1140 T1546.015 T1027.013
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team simulation using the same env-var name (coordinate with offensive security)
  • DFIR / malware-analysis lab hosts intentionally reproducing the sample
  • Test scripts re-using the name MI_V (very unlikely — string is malware-specific)
  • Legacy SAP MI client variables (different name format — MI_V_* with underscore-trailing — keep alert tight to exact MI_V / MI_V2)
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: decode the RegistryValueData (Base64 → UTF-16LE PowerShell) and confirm it contains the Argamal sandbox-check signatures (Sandboxie / Procmon64 enumeration) and bitsadmin download stub. Identify the writing process — typically powershell.exe spawned by a game .exe under user profile. Step 2 — Contain: kill the writing process, delete the env-var (reg delete HKCU\Environment /v MI_V /f and MI_V2), remove any scheduled task referencing %MI_V%/%MI_V2%, and isolate the host. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to the parent process chain (look for ffmpeg.dll/natives2_blob.bin in the same folder), search the org for the originating archive / PixelDrain URL, and check for the {B210D694-...} CLSID hijack on this and peer hosts.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "RegistryValueSet"
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Environment"
| where RegistryValueName in~ ("MI_V","MI_V2")
| extend ValueLen = strlen(tostring(RegistryValueData))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, ValueLen, RegistryValueDataPreview = substring(tostring(RegistryValueData),0,160), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Environment"
| where RegistryValue in~ ("MI_V","MI_V2")
| extend ValueLen = strlen(tostring(RegistryValueData))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, ValueLen, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

Argamal Stage2 BITSAdmin Pull of zaesdl.dat from GitHub AICommand & Control High
Detects bitsadmin.exe invoked with /transfer (or /addfile + /resume) downloading the AES-encrypted RAT payload named zaesdl.dat — Argamal's Stage2 retrieval pattern using GitHub-hosted infrastructure. Rationale: Anchored on the exact payload filename (zaesdl.dat) and Argamal's documented use of GitHub-hosted Stage2 retrieved via bitsadmin. The combination of bitsadmin + github + .dat extension is extremely uncommon outside this family.
ATT&CKT1105 T1197 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using bitsadmin to mirror an artifact from a corporate GitHub Enterprise instance
  • Legacy SCCM / WSUS troubleshooting where an admin manually starts a BITS transfer
  • Red-team using github.com for payload staging (coordinate with the team)
  • Open-source tooling distributing release binaries via raw.githubusercontent.com (verify filename — zaesdl.dat is malware-specific)
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("ccmexec.exe","SCNotification.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "manage.microsoft.com")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture the GitHub URL from the bitsadmin command line and resolve the repo / gist owner; correlate the destination file path with subsequent file writes under %USER%\AppData\Local. Step 2 — Contain: cancel the BITS job (bitsadmin /reset /allusers), quarantine the downloaded .dat / decrypted DLL, kill the spawning PowerShell, and isolate the host. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to the parent chain (PowerShell decoding MI_V env var → bitsadmin), search for the {B210D694-...} CLSID write on this host and peers, and report the GitHub repo to abuse@github.com so the takedown blocks reinfection.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "bitsadmin.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/transfer","/addfile","/create","/resume")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("zaesdl.dat","raw.githubusercontent.com","github.com","gist.githubusercontent.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\bitsadmin.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/transfer","/addfile","/create","/resume")
| where CommandLine has_any ("zaesdl.dat","raw.githubusercontent.com","github.com","gist.githubusercontent.com")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

Argamal RAT C2 Beacon — 186.158.223.35 / freeddns / kozow / ignorelist / UDP-57441 / TCP-3747 AICommand & Control High
Detects connections to the Argamal RAT C2 infrastructure: hardcoded IP 186.158.223.35, the three dyndns FQDNs (asper1.freeddns.org, winst0.kozow.com, country1.ignorelist.com), and the malware's unusual UDP/57441 heartbeat / TCP/3747 extended-mode / UDP/63559 payload-update ports. Rationale: Hardcoded IP 186.158.223.35 plus three named dyndns FQDNs and the three unusual ports (UDP/57441 heartbeat, TCP/3747 extended-mode, UDP/63559 payload-update) are pulled verbatim from the Securelist IOC section. The port-only branch is gated by AppData\Local origin to suppress unrelated egress.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095 T1568.002 T1571
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy game/voice apps using high-numbered UDP ports (suppress by requiring AppData\Local origin)
  • Pen-test infrastructure using freeddns / kozow / ignorelist dyndns providers (coordinate with offensive security)
  • Threat-intel sandbox replaying the C2 IP during a controlled detonation
  • P2P / VPN clients that pick random high ports (filter on InitiatingProcessFolderPath != Program Files)
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "Program Files" and RemotePort in (57441,3747,63559))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify InitiatingProcess (typically rundll32.exe / svchost.exe loading a random-named DLL from %USER%\AppData\Local) and capture connection direction + protocol. Step 2 — Contain: block 186.158.223.35 and the three FQDNs at perimeter and DNS, isolate the host, suspend the loading process, and delete the AppData\Local DLL referenced under the {B210D694-...} CLSID InprocServer32. Step 3 — Hunt: search for any earlier DNS lookups to *.freeddns.org / *.kozow.com / *.ignorelist.com across the fleet, validate the bitsadmin → zaesdl.dat retrieval on the host, and pivot to PixelDrain / AniRena download events in proxy logs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemoteIP == "186.158.223.35")
    or (RemoteUrl in~ ("asper1.freeddns.org","winst0.kozow.com","country1.ignorelist.com"))
    or (RemotePort in (57441,3747,63559) and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "AppData\\Local")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (DstIpAddr == "186.158.223.35")
    or (DstHostname in~ ("asper1.freeddns.org","winst0.kozow.com","country1.ignorelist.com"))
    or (DstPortNumber in (57441,3747,63559))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, NetworkBytes

Argamal Scheduled Task Pointing at AppData\Local DLL via Color System Calibration Loader AIInstallation Medium
Detects scheduled task creation/modification where the Argamal Stage1 PowerShell registers a delayed (3-day) trigger or repurposes the \Microsoft\Windows\WindowsColorSystem\Calibration Loader task to launch a random-named DLL from %USER%\AppData\Local. Catches the persistence and the delayed-detonation primitives in one shot. Rationale: References the exact task path \Microsoft\Windows\WindowsColorSystem\Calibration Loader, the MI_V env-var fed to Stage2, and the AppData\Local DLL target — all article-specific. Catches both the 3-day-delayed task primitive and the recurring login-trigger task in one rule.
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1546.015 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Color management agent re-registering its own Calibration Loader task after an update (verify signer)
  • Sysadmin manually editing a scheduled task for diagnostic purposes
  • Legitimate use of MI_ prefix in non-Argamal scheduled tasks (rare; tighten on exact MI_V or MI_V2)
  • Software inventory tool enumerating tasks (verify it's not invoking /create)
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName == "WindowsUpdate.exe" or InitiatingProcessAccountName endswith "$")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: inspect Get-ScheduledTask -TaskPath "\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsColorSystem\" and any newly created tasks pointing to AppData\Local; capture the DLL target and verify it is not signed by Microsoft. Step 2 — Contain: Unregister-ScheduledTask the malicious task, kill any rundll32/regsvr32 instances loading the AppData DLL, isolate the host. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to the HKCU CLSID {B210D694-...} write event, the MI_V/MI_V2 env var, and the bitsadmin/zaesdl.dat fetch on the same host. Sweep peer hosts for the same task path + AppData DLL signature.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("schtasks.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/create","/change","Register-ScheduledTask","New-ScheduledTask")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Calibration Loader","WindowsColorSystem","MI_V")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "AppData\\Local" and ProcessCommandLine has ".dll" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("rundll32","regsvr32","-Command","-EncodedCommand"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith_cs "\\schtasks.exe" or NewProcessName endswith_cs "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith_cs "\\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/create","/change","Register-ScheduledTask","New-ScheduledTask")
| where CommandLine has_any ("Calibration Loader","WindowsColorSystem","MI_V")
   or (CommandLine has "AppData\\Local" and CommandLine has ".dll")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Argamal Loader Artifacts — natives2_blob.bin / Modified ffmpeg.dll IOC Sweep AIInstallation Medium
Detects the Argamal loader files on disk: the natives2_blob.bin script-executor DLL by filename, the known modified ffmpeg.dll by SHA1 (42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85), and the script-executor DLL by SHA1 (edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d). Triggers on file write, file open, or image load. Rationale: Hash IOC sweep + named-artifact hunt. The filename natives2_blob.bin is unique to Argamal (does not appear in any legitimate ffmpeg / game shipment) and the two SHA1s are confirmed-malicious per the Kaspersky write-up. Union across DeviceFileEvents and DeviceImageLoadEvents catches both the drop and the load.
ATT&CKT1574.001 T1204.002 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandbox / malware-analysis lab handling the sample (expected — exclude analyst hostnames)
  • DFIR engineer copying the IOC into a quarantine share for review
  • Threat-intel-feed sync writing the hash into a defensive tooling repo (path-suppress)
  • Initial Kaspersky telemetry replay during deployment validation
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "AnalystSandbox" or DeviceName startswith "MALWARE-LAB-")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the writing process is a game executable (RenPy / RPG Maker MV runner) under a user-writable folder, and that ffmpeg.dll alongside has the matching modified SHA1. Step 2 — Contain: quarantine the entire game archive folder, kill the game process and any child PowerShell, isolate the host, and remove the {B210D694-...}/{722D0F89-...} CLSID overrides + MI_V env var. Step 3 — Hunt: trace the download URL (PixelDrain / AniRena), sweep the org for other hosts with natives2_blob.bin or the ffmpeg.dll SHA1, and pivot on the user account for prior torrent / adult-game-catalogue web activity in proxy logs.
union
  (DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where FileName =~ "natives2_blob.bin" or SHA1 in~ ("42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85","edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="FileEvent", ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA1, FileOriginUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where FileName =~ "ffmpeg.dll" and SHA1 == "42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="ImageLoad", ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA1, FileOriginUrl="", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where SHA1 == "edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="ImageLoad", ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA1, FileOriginUrl="", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "natives2_blob.bin"
    or TargetFileSHA1 in~ ("42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85","edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA1, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85", "edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d") or SHA1 in~ ("42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85", "edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d") or MD5 in~ ("42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85", "edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85", "edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d") or SHA1 in~ ("42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85", "edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d") or MD5 in~ ("42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85", "edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85", "edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing campaign

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-03 20 use cases 6 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

A large-scale npm supply chain attack compromised over 90 versions of @redhat-cloud-services packages, silently infecting CI/CD environments and developer systems. The malicious code steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines, then spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages. Discover how the attack works, what data is at risk, and the steps you can take to protect your organization. The post Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing campaign appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Passwordless sudo rule dropped into /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma privilege escalation) · [LLM] Security vendor domain blackhole written to /etc/hosts from non-admin process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing cam
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Bun runtime spawned via node→shell→bun chain from npm install (Miasma dropper) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping (Miasma payload) · [LLM] Cloud IMDS credential harvesting from node/bun process on CI runner · [LLM] Public GitHub repo creation matching Miasma 'adjective-creature-N' exfil pattern · [LLM] Worm-injected .github/setup.js commit with 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]' message · [LLM] Destructive 'rm -rf ~' or Miasma honeytoken tripwire from node/bun process tree · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Bun runtime spawned via node→shell→bun chain from npm install (Miasma dropper) AIInstallation High
Hunts the signature process tree of the Red Hat npm Miasma campaign: a node.js process spawning a shell that spawns the Bun runtime, typically from npm preinstall hooks. This is the exact anti-Node-monitoring evasion chain the article identifies for the 4.29 MB index.js dropper. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact statement: 'creating an unusual process chain (node → shell → bun → payload) designed to evade Node-focused monitoring.' The Bun runtime is downloaded to a temp path before execution, and bun is not a standard CI runner tool — the parent-of-parent being node/npm in a preinstall context is article-specific.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate developer running 'bun run' inside their local project that was bootstrapped via npm install scripts
  • CI pipelines that have intentionally adopted Bun as their JS runtime (e.g. via 'bun install' wrapper scripts that call node first)
  • Bun official installer (curl bun.sh/install | bash) executed by an admin
  • Internal monorepo tooling that proxies node through shell wrappers to invoke bun
  • Docker buildkit layers running bun in /tmp for ephemeral compile steps
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "bun-baseline-pipeline" or InitiatingProcessParentCommandLine has "bun-baseline-pipeline")
| where not (DeviceName has "buildkit" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "docker-buildkit")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: pivot on InitiatingProcessParentCommandLine for the npm package name and version; correlate with DeviceFileEvents for the index.js write that immediately preceded execution — cross-check the SHA256 against 7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655 / b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966. 2. CONTAIN: isolate the runner/dev host, revoke its GitHub Actions OIDC tokens and any npm publish PATs scoped to the user, rotate cloud IMDS-reachable role credentials. 3. HUNT: pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound bun.sh downloads and api.github.com posts from the same DeviceId, and to CloudAppEvents for repo creation under the user's GitHub account in the next 60 minutes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("bun", "bun.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","npm","npm-cli.js","yarn","pnpm")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall","npm install","index.js")
| where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath startswith "/home/runner/" or FolderPath has "/.bun/" or FolderPath has @"\AppData\Local\Temp\" or FolderPath has "/var/folders/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
    ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
    GrandparentFile = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "bun.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "sh" or ParentProcessName endswith "bash" or ParentProcessName endswith "cmd.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "powershell.exe"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node","npm","preinstall","index.js")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/","/home/runner/","/.bun/",@"\AppData\Local\Temp\","/var/folders/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bun Runtime Spawned by Node Shell Chain (Miasma npm Dropper)
id: a3f9d8e2-7b41-4c5a-9e2d-1f8b6c3a9d77
description: Detects the node → shell → bun process chain characteristic of the Red Hat npm Miasma supply chain campaign, where a preinstall hook executes a 4.29 MB index.js dropper that downloads and detonates the Bun runtime.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1546.016
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bun'
      - '/bun.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  selection_grandparent_or_path:
    - ParentCommandLine|contains:
        - 'node'
        - 'npm'
        - 'preinstall'
        - 'index.js'
    - Image|contains:
        - '/tmp/'
        - '/home/runner/'
        - '/.bun/'
        - '\Temp\'
        - '/var/folders/'
  condition: selection_image and selection_parent and selection_grandparent_or_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer use of Bun in npm scripts (rare in CI baseline)
  - Bun installer running interactively (curl https://bun.sh/install | bash)
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.name:bun OR @process.name:bun.exe OR @Image:(*\bun OR *\bun.exe OR */bun OR */bun.exe)) (@process.parent.name:(sh OR bash OR dash OR zsh OR cmd.exe OR powershell.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*\sh OR *\bash OR *\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe)) (@process.command_line:(*node* OR *npm* OR *preinstall* OR *index.js*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*node* OR *npm* OR *preinstall* OR *index.js*)) (@process.executable.path:(*/tmp/* OR */home/runner/* OR */.bun/* OR */var/folders/*) OR @Image:(*\Temp\* OR */tmp/* OR */.bun/*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/bun(\.exe)?$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(sh|bash|dash|zsh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe)$/i
| regex("(node|npm|preinstall|index\\.js)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| regex("(\/tmp\/|\/home\/runner\/|\.bun\/|\\\\Temp\\\\|\/var\/folders\/)", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName, ParentCommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="bun" OR Processes.process_name="bun.exe") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash" OR Processes.parent_process_name="dash" OR Processes.parent_process_name="zsh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="powershell.exe") AND (Processes.parent_process="*node*" OR Processes.parent_process="*npm*" OR Processes.parent_process="*preinstall*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping (Miasma payload) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma payload's runtime-secret theft technique: scanning /proc/<pid>/cmdline for 'Runner.Worker' to locate the GitHub Actions worker PID, then extracting masked Actions secrets from process memory via a distinctive grep regex for '"isSecret":true' JSON tokens. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim code block: 'findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux', the exact extraction regex 'grep -aoE \'"[^"]+":{"value":"[^"]*","isSecret":true}\'', and the /proc/<pid>/cmdline scan strategy. These strings have no legitimate occurrence outside this campaign and the article explicitly cites them as the runner-memory exfiltration mechanism.
ATT&CKT1003 T1552.005 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • GitHub Actions runner internal diagnostic scripts walking /proc (parent should be Runner.Listener)
  • Security tooling like osquery or auditbeat scanning /proc/<pid>/cmdline for inventory
  • SOC IR scripts performing memory triage that grep for 'isSecret' patterns
  • Legitimate Docker/Kubernetes diagnostic containers scanning process tree on the runner
  • Custom CI debug steps echoing masked secrets to logs (the regex marker would appear in logs but not in process args)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !endswith "Runner.Listener"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("osqueryd","auditbeat","falcon-sensor")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: capture the full process tree and confirm parent is NOT Runner.Listener / actions.runner.worker; pull the cmdline and check for the exact 'isSecret' regex which has no legitimate runtime use. 2. CONTAIN: terminate the offending PID, freeze the runner VM/container, rotate ALL secrets exposed to ANY workflow run on that runner within the last 30 days (GitHub org/repo/env secrets, OIDC-trusted cloud roles). 3. HUNT: pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound api.github.com PUT/POST traffic from the runner immediately after the scrape, and to GitHub audit logs for unexpected repo creation under the maintainer account.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker", "findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux", "\"isSecret\":true")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "grep" and ProcessCommandLine has "-aoE" and ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "cmdline")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "cmdline" and ProcessCommandLine has "tr -d")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("runner-worker","Runner.Listener","actions.runner")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
    InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker", "findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux", "\"isSecret\":true")
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "grep" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "-aoE" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "cmdline")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "Runner.Listener"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GitHub Actions Runner.Worker Memory Scraping (Miasma)
id: 5e7c2d91-3b48-4a67-bc1e-9d4f7a8e6c52
description: Detects scraping of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process memory for masked secrets, using the regex pattern '"isSecret":true' on /proc/<pid>/cmdline reads. Specific to the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing campaign.

Cloud IMDS credential harvesting from node/bun process on CI runner AIActions on Objectives High
Detects short-lived node or bun processes contacting the AWS/Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254) or GCP metadata service (metadata.google.internal) — the Miasma payload's mechanism for stealing instance role credentials, Azure IMDS OAuth2 tokens, and GCP service-account tokens from CI runners. Rationale: Anchored on the article's credential-theft section listing exact endpoints: 'IMDS (169.254.169.254)', 'metadata.google.internal service-account tokens', and 'IMDS OAuth2 tokens for management.azure.com, graph.microsoft.com, and Key Vault (*.vault.azure.net)'. Node/bun calling IMDS from a CI runner is the article's specific behavior — the article notes Linux CI runners as the primary target.
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1528 T1552.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS SDK v3 in Node.js apps legitimately calling IMDS to resolve instance role credentials on EC2
  • Bun-based Lambda runtime adapters or Vercel/Netlify Edge functions querying their host metadata
  • Kubernetes IRSA workloads where the SDK contacts the IMDS proxy
  • Azure Functions custom containers using @azure/identity DefaultAzureCredential
  • GCP Cloud Run / GKE workloads using google-auth-library to resolve service-account credentials
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("aws-sdk","@azure/identity","google-auth-library")
| where DeviceName !startswith "baseline-sdk-app"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: pivot on InitiatingProcessCommandLine to confirm the node/bun process is not a known SDK-using app (check against ServiceNow CMDB inventory); look for parent process being npm/preinstall and IMDS calls within seconds of process start. 2. CONTAIN: rotate the IMDS-exposed role credentials on the affected host immediately (AWS: IAM revoke-active-sessions; Azure: revoke managed identity tokens; GCP: rotate service account key), then quarantine the host. 3. HUNT: in CloudTrail/AzureActivity/GCP audit, pivot on the leaked role principal for AssumeRole / API activity from non-instance IPs in the 24h after the call — a key Miasma exfil signal is the credentials being used from attacker infrastructure.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254" or RemoteUrl has_any ("metadata.google.internal", "169.254.169.254", "metadata.azure.com", ".vault.azure.net")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","bun","bun.exe")
| summarize EndpointsHit = make_set(RemoteUrl), IPHits = make_set(RemoteIP), HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where HitCount >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254" or DstHostname has_any ("metadata.google.internal","metadata.azure.com",".vault.azure.net")
| where Url has_any ("node","bun") or DstHostname has_any ("metadata","vault.azure")
| summarize EndpointsHit = make_set(DstHostname), HitCount = count() by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, NetworkApplicationProtocol
| order by HitCount desc
title: Cloud IMDS Access by Node or Bun Process (Miasma Harvester)
id: 8b1c4e72-5d39-4f86-a2b1-7e3c9f5a4d18
description: Detects node or bun processes contacting cloud instance metadata endpoints (AWS IMDS 169.254.169.254, GCP metadata.google.internal, Azure IMDS, Key Vault) to harvest temporary cloud credentials. Specific to the Red Hat npm Miasma campaign on CI runners and developer hosts.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1552.005
  - attack.t1528
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '/bun'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
  selection_dest:
    DestinationIp:
      - '169.254.169.254'
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'metadata.google.internal'
      - 'metadata.azure.com'
      - '.vault.azure.net'
  condition: selection_process and selection_dest
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Node.js apps using AWS SDK / Azure SDK that resolve IMDS for instance role credentials
  - Bun-based serverless adapters that intentionally call IMDS
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon OR cloudtrail) (@network.destination.ip:169.254.169.254 OR @DestinationIp:169.254.169.254 OR @network.destination.host:(metadata.google.internal OR metadata.azure.com) OR @DestinationHostname:(metadata.google.internal OR *.vault.azure.net)) (@process.name:(node OR bun) OR @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\bun.exe OR */node OR */bun))

| ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|bun)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, action, bytes
| filter dstAddr = "169.254.169.254"

| stats count(*) as imdsCalls, sum(bytes) as totalBytes by srcAddr, bin(5m)
| sort @timestamp desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="169.254.169.254" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="metadata.google.internal") AND (All_Traffic.process_name="node" OR All_Traffic.process_name="node.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
